Q: Create new column in yf dataframe not possible? A:

New version of yfinance returns the data in a MultiIndex column structure way. Flattening df['Close'] and spy fixes it

Try this

import yfinance as yf

df = yf.download("NVDA", period="3y", interval="1wk")
spy = yf.download("SPY", period="3y", interval="1wk")

df.columns = df.columns.get_level_values(0)
spy.columns = spy.columns.get_level_values(0)

df['RS_Ratio'] = df['Close'] / spy['Close']

print(df[['Close', 'RS_Ratio']])
print("\nRS_Ratio stats:")
print(df['RS_Ratio'].describe())

Q: Why am I experiencing DNS resolution failures only in the final stage of a multi-stage Docker Compose build? A:

I never figured out what the problem was, but I suspect it's some emergent interaction between docker, compose, buildx, and the awful, debilitating coupling of Ubuntu, Snap, and AppArmor.

I removed Xubuntu 24.04 and installed Arch and the DNS resolution failures no longer occur, for the exact same code.

Docker versions I am now using, and without Snap and AppArmor, and no issues are present:

Q: Is it possible to know last time a Row was updated in a table or view in Snowflake? A:

Use row timestamps to measure latency in your pipelines:

Row timestamps provide a precise, chronological record of when each row in a table was last updated. Rows modified in the same transaction share the exact same timestamp and rows modified in different transactions are ordered by when they were committed.

After row timestamps are enabled, tables expose the METADATA$ROW_LAST_COMMIT_TIME column, which returns the timestamp when each row was last modified. This enables change tracking, incremental processing, and time-travel queries based on row modification time.

CREATE TABLE tab(id INT, col STRING)
  ROW_TIMESTAMP = TRUE;

INSERT INTO tab(id, col)
VALUES (1, 'a');

SELECT METADATA$ROW_LAST_COMMIT_TIME, id, col
FROM tab;
/*
METADATA$ROW_LAST_COMMIT_TIME   ID  COL
2026-02-21 21:09:16.322 +0100   1   a
*/

UPDATE tab
SET col = 'b'
WHERE id = 1;

SELECT METADATA$ROW_LAST_COMMIT_TIME, id, col
FROM tab;
/*
METADATA$ROW_LAST_COMMIT_TIME   ID  COL
2026-02-21 21:10:50.925 +0100   1   b
*/

Q: pip always fails ssl verification A:

Look for SSL_CERT_FILE or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE variables on your path. It is very likely that they are pointing to the wrong cert file. You can simply unset them and try again.
